init.label: Decision Matrix
init.body:
# Weighted scoring, ranked
A **Decision Matrix** scores a table of options against weighted criteria and ranks them.

**Flow:** a Frame of scores (rows are options, the first text column names them, number columns are criteria) → the **Decision Matrix** node → `Option · Score · Rank`, best first.

Each criterion gets a row on the node: a **weight** (default 1; negative = lower is better, like Price) and a **Norm** override. Score = **Σ(value × weight) / Σ|weight|**. Tweak a weight and watch the ranking move.

init.label: Mixed scales, one range
init.body:
Price is in **dollars**; the rest are out of **10**. Scored raw, Price would swamp everything, so every criterion is normalized onto a common **0–1** range and the **weights**, not the raw scales, decide influence.

The default here is **÷Max**. Price alone overrides to **Rank** in its row: rank keeps only the order, so one runaway price can't dominate.

**Breakdown** is on: each criterion column is its **signed contribution**, and the contributions sum to the Score. Price shows negative, the penalty it is.

init.label: The podium is a chart
init.body: The ranking is already the table. For the podium, **Select Columns** keeps `Laptop · Score`, and a two-column frame into **Chart** draws labeled bars: the first column names them, the second sets the lengths.

init.label: Sensitivity
init.body:
# Stress-test the weights
The winner depends on the weights picked above. **Sensitivity** re-scores the same options under several weight **scenarios**, one per row of the Scenarios frame, and returns a **Cube**: per scenario the **Winner**, the **Margin** (top score minus runner-up), and the full **Ranking** nested in the cell. Drill in.

The winner flips: **UltraSlim** under Balanced, **PowerLifter** when performance dominates. Under Budget the Winner cell reads **UltraSlim = Budget**, a dead tie at Margin 0. That pick is fragile; the first two hold.
